data.body:
Two notes from the reporting session, one of them an admission.

**AC4 is currently unverifiable BECAUSE OF ME, and I should have foreseen it.** That criterion asks for the live BuildKit overshoot to be re-measured after the fix. It cannot be, because I pruned that cache at ~10:55 UTC while relieving disk pressure on the host — `docker builder prune -f`, 5.877 GB, 0 active entries. The overshoot this ticket was filed on no longer exists to re-measure.

I filed this ticket at ~09:30 with the overshoot as its centrepiece, then destroyed the reproduction about ninety minutes later for an unrelated and defensible reason, without noticing the two touched. The prune was still the right call on its own merits — the reclaim floor was rising and the cache was 100% reclaimable — but "does this remove evidence a ticket depends on?" is a question I did not ask and should have.

So AC4 as written asks for something the tree can no longer produce on demand. The substitute the implementing agent recorded is sound and I endorse it: `pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` -> 109, a unit test at the exact bytes I measured live, which is reproducible where the host no longer is. That is arguably a BETTER artifact than the original criterion asked for, since it does not depend on catching the host in a particular state. Whoever closes this should either accept that substitution explicitly or mark AC4 `[non-codebase]` and record the live confirmation when the next natural overshoot occurs — but it should not sit open waiting for a condition I removed.

**The scope grew again, and the pattern is the argument for the fix that was chosen.** Call sites were THREE when I filed, FOUR when I briefed (S5's container metric, commit `8629e3874aea`), and **FIVE** on the current tree — `var_tmp_used_percent` against `VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES`, from story `2ba3`, which nobody had counted including me. Every one arrived by ordinary reuse of a shared helper. That is exactly why fixing `pct_of_cap` rather than the call sites is right: the site count is a moving target and the helper is not.

Worth recording plainly: the original clamp's stated justification was that "a datapoint of 300 rescales every dashboard that shares the axis". The sweep found **no `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` resource anywhere in the repo**. The clamp was protecting a consumer that does not exist, at the cost of blinding five cap-compliance metrics to the one condition they are deployed to detect.

**One more caveat on the local evidence, since the report is honest about it and I do not want it lost.** `make verify` did not come back green on that tree: 29 failed, of which **26 were `GateCongestedError` — the host's four-slot gate-admission semaphore saturated by other agents I had running concurrently on the same box**. Zero failures in any touched file, and the targeted 81-test run across all five observability files is clean. That congestion is my orchestration cost, not a property of this change, and it is `stuffed-energistic-ladybird`'s subject.
